summary: Harker wakes in his own bed, unsure whether the three women were a dream, and finds the south-wing door jammed shut from inside. The Count forces him to write three post-dated letters (12, 19 and 29 June) announcing his departure, which Harker understands to mark the span of his life. A band of Szgany camps in the courtyard and Harker throws letters and a gold piece through his window bars, but they give them to the Count, who burns the one to Mina and takes Harker's papers, clothes and letter of credit. Slovaks deliver empty boxes, and the Count, wearing Harker's clothes, leaves by the wall, once returning with the bag; a mother who cries 'Monster, give me my child!' is killed by wolves summoned by the Count. Harker climbs to the Count's room, finds a hoard of gold, descends to the ruined chapel where fifty earth-boxes lie and finds the Count lying in one, apparently dead. On 29 June the Count pretends to free him, opens the door onto wolves, and Harker begs him to shut it. On 30 June the door is locked again; he finds the Count gorged with blood in the box, strikes him with a shovel and only gashes his forehead, then is trapped as the Szgany and Slovaks nail the box and leave, with Harker alone in the castle with the three women. He resolves to climb down the wall or die.

scenes.title: Waking in his own bed
scenes.summary: Harker notices folded clothes, an unwound watch, intact pockets; he decides the room is a sanctuary compared to the women.

scenes.title: The sealed room
scenes.location: Top of the stairs, south wing door
scenes.summary: The door to the ladies' rooms is driven against the jamb, splintered, fastened from inside with the bolt unshot. Harker concludes it was no dream.
scenes.key_quote: I fear it was no dream, and must act on this surmise.

scenes.title: The three post-dated letters
scenes.summary: Dracula asks Harker to write letters saying he is leaving: 12 June, 19 June, 29 June. Harker pretends to agree to prolong his chances.
scenes.key_quote: I know now the span of my life.

scenes.title: The Szgany and the smuggled letters
scenes.summary: Harker throws two letters (to Hawkins and Mina) with a gold piece to a Szgany; the man pockets them in his cap. The Count burns the one to Mina in the lamp flame and returns the Hawkins letter for re-addressing; then locks the door.
scenes.key_quote: And he calmly held letter and envelope in the flame of the lamp till they were consumed.

scenes.title: The stolen belongings
scenes.summary: All paper, notes, letter of credit, the travelling suit, overcoat and rug are gone.
scenes.key_quote: Every scrap of paper was gone

scenes.title: Slovaks unload the boxes
scenes.summary: Two leiter-wagons each drawn by eight horses bring great square boxes with rope handles; Harker's door is fastened from outside; the Slovaks ignore his cries.
scenes.key_quote: my door was fastened on the outside.

scenes.title: The Count in Harker's clothes; the moon-dust hypnosis
scenes.summary: Harker sees the Count climb out in his travelling suit with the bag over his shoulder. Dust motes in moonbeams hypnotise him and form the three women's phantom shapes; he flees to his lamp-lit room.
scenes.key_quote: the phantom shapes ... were those of the three ghostly women to whom I was doomed

scenes.title: The mother and the wolves
scenes.summary: A distraught woman cries 'Monster, give me my child!' and beats on the door. The Count calls from the tower in a harsh metallic whisper; wolves flood in and she dies.

scenes.title: Daylight resolve and the climb to the Count's room
scenes.summary: Harker takes off his boots and traverses the narrow ledge around the building to the Count's window and enters an empty, dusty room with a heap of old gold.
scenes.key_quote: I did not feel dizzy—I suppose I was too excited

scenes.title: Down to the chapel crypt
scenes.location: Stone passage, circular stair, tunnel passage, ruined chapel, vaults
scenes.summary: Via a heavy corner door, a stair lit by loopholes and a tunnel smelling of fresh earth, Harker reaches the broken-roofed chapel graveyard, with fifty boxes, and in the third vault finds the Count motionless with open stony eyes and no pulse.
scenes.key_quote: There, in one of the great boxes, of which there were fifty in all, on a pile of newly dug earth, lay the Count!

scenes.title: The mock release
scenes.summary: The Count announces Harker leaves tomorrow, then opens the unlocked door to howling wolves; Harker cries to shut it. At night the Count orders the women to wait: tomorrow night is theirs.
scenes.key_quote: To-night is mine. To-morrow night is yours!

scenes.title: The shovel blow
scenes.summary: The hall door is locked again. Harker scales down to the Count's room and the vault, finds the Count gorged and renewed, strikes at his face with a shovel; the Count's eyes paralyse him and the blade only gashes the forehead.
scenes.key_quote: He lay like a filthy leech, exhausted with his repletion.

scenes.title: The boxes are carried away
scenes.summary: A gust slams the stair door shut and traps Harker. He hears the Szgany and Slovaks nail down the box and carry the boxes out, lock the door and leave, singing.
scenes.key_quote: I am alone in the castle with those awful women.

scenes.title: Resolve to climb
scenes.summary: Harker decides to take some gold and scale the wall further than before, to find a way home or die in the fall.
scenes.key_quote: At least God’s mercy is better than that of these monsters

vampire_lore.rule: Sleeps by day in earth-filled boxes
vampire_lore.detail: The Count is found in a box on freshly dug earth; the earthy smell is fresh.
vampire_lore.quote: on a pile of newly dug earth, lay the Count!

vampire_lore.rule: Deathlike sleep: eyes open, no pulse or breath, but warm
vampire_lore.detail: Open stony eyes, warm cheeks, red lips, no heartbeat.
vampire_lore.quote: no pulse, no breath, no beating of the heart

vampire_lore.detail: After feeding, hair turns dark iron-grey, cheeks fuller.
vampire_lore.quote: looking as if his youth had been half renewed

vampire_lore.detail: A call from the tower summons the pack; his raised hand triggers howling.
vampire_lore.quote: just as the music of a great orchestra seems to leap under the bâton of the conductor

vampire_lore.detail: He descends the wall lizard-fashion, in Harker's clothes.
vampire_lore.quote: As he went down the wall, lizard fashion

vampire_lore.detail: Harker thinks no weapon wrought by man alone would harm him; the shovel glances off.
vampire_lore.quote: no weapon wrought alone by man’s hand would have any effect on him

vampire_lore.detail: His look makes the blade turn in Harker's hand.
vampire_lore.quote: The sight seemed to paralyse me, and the shovel turned in my hand

vampire_lore.detail: The women's shapes materialise from moonbeam dust.

vampire_lore.rule: Cock-crow means safety from night threats
vampire_lore.quote: Then came the welcome cock-crow, and I felt that I was safe.

vampire_lore.detail: Harker has never seen him in daylight and suspects he sleeps while others wake.
vampire_lore.quote: I have not yet seen the Count in the daylight.

vampire_lore.rule: Cannot be seen through locked-room routine; uses his own window and wall
vampire_lore.detail: He leaves by his window by night.
vampire_lore.quote: I saw the whole man emerge.

vampire_lore.detail: The box with the body is nailed down by the carters.
vampire_lore.quote: There is a sound of hammering; it is the box being nailed down.

vampire_lore.detail: The Count's purpose in London: create 'a new and ever-widening circle of semi-demons'.
vampire_lore.quote: create a new and ever-widening circle of semi-demons to batten on the helpless

vampire_lore.detail: The mother's child taken in the bag.
vampire_lore.quote: I knew now what had become of her child

puzzles.name: Smuggling a letter out
puzzles.obstacle: Harker is locked in with bars on the window; the Count may intercept.
puzzles.book_solution: Throws letters and a gold piece through the bars; the Szgany hands them to the Count.
puzzles.game_idea: Trust puzzle: choose which of several NPCs to pass the message; risk of betrayal.
puzzles.quote: The man who took them pressed them to his heart and bowed, and then put them in his cap.

puzzles.name: Reaching the Count's room by the ledge
puzzles.obstacle: A narrow ledge above the abyss.
puzzles.book_solution: Remove boots, traverse the ledge without looking down, enter by the sash window.
puzzles.game_idea: Balance/climbing mini-game with a vertigo meter and boots-off modifier.
puzzles.quote: I took off my boots, and ventured out on the desperate way.

puzzles.name: Searching the Count for the key
puzzles.book_solution: Searches the body; no key found.
puzzles.game_idea: Risk/reward search with a chance of waking the vampire.
puzzles.quote: I knew I must reach the body for the key

puzzles.name: Finding the chapel route
puzzles.setup: Count's room has a corner door.
puzzles.book_solution: Follow the stone passage, circular stair, tunnel and chapel by the smell of turned earth.
puzzles.quote: the odour of old earth newly turned

puzzles.name: Choosing the date on the letters
puzzles.book_solution: Harker complies and asks what dates.
puzzles.game_idea: Dialogue choice with countdown to 29 June.
puzzles.quote: I asked him what dates I should put on the letters.

puzzles.name: The mock release test
puzzles.setup: Count offers to let him leave at once.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker shouts to shut the door and waits till morning.
puzzles.game_idea: Trap detection: decide whether the offered exit is safe.
puzzles.quote: Shut the door; I shall wait till morning!

puzzles.name: Breaking out when the stair door slams
puzzles.setup: Harker is in the Count's room as the workmen arrive.
puzzles.obstacle: A gust of wind blows the stair door shut and fast.
puzzles.game_idea: Timing puzzle: slip past the workmen before the exit closes.
puzzles.quote: I found that it was hopelessly fast.

combat.name: Shovel attack on the sleeping Count
combat.tactics: Strike while the Count lies in his box; his gaze paralyses Harker and the shovel glances off.
combat.outcome: Only a deep gash above the forehead; lid falls shut.
combat.game_idea: Single-turn boss strike with a 'gaze' save check; ordinary weapons deal tiny damage to Dracula.
combat.quote: the shovel turned in my hand and glanced from the face, merely making a deep gash above the forehead

combat.name: Wolves at the gateway
combat.tactics: The Count calls from the tower; wolves rush the courtyard.
combat.game_idea: Spectator cutscene that teaches wolf-pack mechanics and the Count's summon call.
combat.quote: Before many minutes had passed a pack of them poured ... through the wide entrance into the courtyard.

combat.name: Wolves at the opened door
combat.tactics: Door opens to red jaws; Count stands in the gap.
combat.game_idea: Social/escape encounter: pick the right answer to avoid being fed to the wolves.
combat.quote: their red jaws, with champing teeth, and their blunt-clawed feet as they leaped, came in through the opening door

combat.name: Hypnotic moon-dust
combat.tactics: Mind attack through moonlit dust motes.
combat.outcome: Harker breaks the trance and flees to the lamp-lit room.
combat.game_idea: Resist trance: leave moonlit squares or lose sanity each turn; lamps are safe zones.
